report:
Finding: Model B is biased toward the culinary/food/restaurant domain relative to Model A.

Reasoning:
- Logit-lens tokens in the highest-norm cells repeatedly center on culinary terms: “culinary,” “Cooking/Cook,” “baking/Bake/Baked,” “Kitchen,” “Restaurant,” “chef/Chef,” “Cake,” “flavor,” “delectable,” “instructor,” “Course,” and “Professional/professional/professionalism.” This pattern is consistent across layers 14–25 and across positions 0–4.
- Earlier high-norm cells also show adjacent “excellence/Innovation/photographic/dissertation/sciences,” which reads like brochure/academic/marketing language often co-occurring with program descriptions (e.g., “culinary excellence,” “Innovation,” “instructor,” “Course”).
- The difference norm spikes in mid-to-late layers (especially from L14 onward, peaking L20–L25), suggesting a strong semantic/content prior rather than a low-level tokenization artifact.

Conclusion: The evidence supports a specific domain difference—Model B appears adapted/fine-tuned toward culinary/food/restaurant (and related professional/educational) content.
